$comment: The JSON-LD context for the AWR/2 namespace, served at
WHAT IT IS FOR, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. The eddsa-jcs-2022 proof canonicalizes JSON with
RFC 8785 and never expands JSON-LD, so NO verifier needs this document and SPEC.md
13.5 forbids fetching it during verification. It exists for the other kind of
consumer -- one that expands the JSON-LD, for example to load AWR documents into a
graph store alongside other Verifiable Credentials. Until this file was written the
namespace URI returned the verifier's HTML page from an SPA fallback, so such a
consumer got text/html where it asked for a context: worse than a 404, because it
Every term is @protected: a document cannot redefine `outputDigest` to mean something
else and still expand under this context. Terms are typed where the type is fixed by
the specification -- @id for identifiers, xsd:dateTime for timestamps, xsd:integer
for latencyMs -- and left as plain strings where SPEC.md 4.3 deliberately carries a
decimal as a string rather than a number.

Five terms are deliberately NOT defined here — `digestSRI`, `evidence`, `status`, `nonce` and `name`. The VC 2.0 context already defines and @protects all five, and redefining a protected term makes expansion fail outright rather than degrade. Ours carry the same meaning in every case, so they are reused rather than shadowed. The list was computed by diffing our term set against the VC 2.0 context, not guessed: three of the five were found only after expansion failed on 12 of 15 valid vectors.
